complete_actual_units.text: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Behold, now the kingdom will return to David’s house.
If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the Lord’s house in Jerusalem, the people’s heart will return to the Lord and their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me.”
The king took counsel, went, and made two golden heifers. He said to the people, “Let your going up to Jerusalem be enough. Behold, your gods, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt!”
He placed one in Bethel and put the other in Dan.
This matter became a sin. The people went before the one as far as Dan.
He made houses on high places and appointed some of the people as priests who were not from the sons of Levi.

Jeroboam held a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast in the land of Judah, and went up onto the altar he had made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers he had made. He stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places he had made.

He went up onto the altar he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, at the feast he had fashioned from his heart. He held a feast for the sons of Israel and went up onto the altar to offer sacrifice.
Behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the Lord’s word, while Jeroboam stood at the altar to offer sacrifice.

He called to the altar by the Lord’s word: “Altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. He will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you.”
He gave a portent that day, saying, “This is the word the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar will split, and the fat upon it will pour out.”

When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had called against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” Behold, the hand he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
The altar split, and the fat poured from the altar, according to the portent the man of God had given by the Lord’s word.
for the king is dead.” They came to Samaria and buried the king in Samaria.
They washed the chariot at Samaria’s spring. Swine and dogs licked the blood, and prostitutes bathed in the blood, according to the Lord’s word which He had spoken.
The rest of Ahab’s acts, all he did, the ivory house he built, and all the cities he made—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
The child Samuel ministered to the Lord before Eli the priest. The Lord’s word was precious in those days; there was no distinct vision.
At that time Eli was sleeping in his place. His eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see,
and it was before God’s lamp was put in order. Samuel was sleeping in the sanctuary where God’s ark was,
and the Lord called, “Samuel, Samuel!” He said, “Here I am.”
David said to Saul, “Let my lord’s heart not collapse because of him. Your servant will go and fight this foreigner.”
Saul said to David, “You certainly cannot go against the foreigner to fight him. You are a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
David said to Saul, “Your servant tended his father’s flock. Whenever a lion or a bear came and took a sheep from the herd,
I went after it, struck it, and pulled the sheep from its mouth. If it rose against me, I seized its throat, struck it, and killed it.

Your servant struck both bear and lion. The uncircumcised foreigner will be like one of them. Shall I not go and strike him and remove disgrace from Israel today? For who is this uncircumcised man who has defied the battle line of the living God?
The Lord, who rescued me from the lion’s paw and the bear’s paw, will rescue me from this uncircumcised foreigner’s hand.” Saul said to David, “Go, and the Lord will be with you.”
Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him at Armathaim, in his city. Saul had removed the mediums and the knowers from the land.
The foreigners gathered, came, and camped at Soman. Saul gathered every man of Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
Saul saw the foreigners’ camp and was afraid, and his heart was greatly astounded.
Saul inquired through the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him by dreams, by clear signs, or by prophets.
Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so that I may go to her and inquire through her.” His servants said to him, “There is a woman who is a medium at Endor.”
Elisha came to Damascus, and the son of Ader, king of Syria, was ill. They reported to him, saying, ‘The man of God has come here.’
The king said to Hazael, ‘Take a manaa in your hand and go to meet the man of God. Inquire of the Lord through him, saying, Will I recover from this illness of mine?’

Hazael went to meet him, taking a manaa in his hand and all the good things of Damascus, a load for forty camels. He came and stood before him and said to Elisha, ‘Your son, the son of Ader, king of Syria, sent me to you, saying, Will I recover from this illness of mine?’
Elisha said, ‘Go, tell him: You will surely live. And the Lord has shown me that you will surely die.’
He stood before his face and held it until shame, and the man of God wept.

Hazael said, ‘Why does my lord weep?’ He said, ‘Because I know all the evils you will do to the sons of Israel: you will send their strongholds into fire, kill their chosen men with the sword, dash down their infants, and tear open their pregnant women.’
Hazael said, ‘Who is your slave, a dead dog, that he should do this thing?’ Elisha said, ‘The Lord has shown me you reigning over Syria.’
He went away from Elisha and entered his master’s presence. He said to him, ‘What did Elisha say to you?’ He said, ‘He told me, You will surely live.’
The next day he took the machma, dipped it in the water, and wrapped it over his face. He died, and Hazael became king in his place.
Sellum son of Jabis became king. In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Sellum reigned a month of days in Samaria.
Manaem son of Gaddi went up from Tharsila, came to Samaria, struck Sellum son of Jabis in Samaria, and put him to death.
The rest of Sellum’s deeds and the conspiracy he formed—behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
Then Manaem struck Thersa, everything in it, and its territory from Thersa, because they did not open to him. He struck it and ripped open the pregnant women.
This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,
and all the Israelites who clothed themselves in words that were not so against the Lord their God, built themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.
They set up pillars and groves for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
They burned incense there at all the high places like the nations whom the Lord deported before them. They made associates and engraved, to provoke the Lord.
They served the idols, concerning which the Lord had said to them, ‘You shall not do this thing to the Lord.’

The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all His prophets, every seer: ‘Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My ordinances, and all the law I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them through My servants the prophets.’
But they did not listen. They hardened their back more than the back of their fathers.

They did not keep His testimonies by which He warned them. They followed vain things and became vain, and followed the nations around them, concerning whom He had commanded them not to do such things.
They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God. They made a casting for themselves, two heifers, made groves, bowed down to all heaven’s host, and served Baal.
They led their sons and daughters through fire, practiced divinations, read omens, and were sold to do evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.
The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence. None remained except the tribe of Judah alone.

Moreover, he tore down the altar at Bethel, the high place Jeroboam son of Nabat had made, who caused Israel to sin—both that altar and the high place. He shattered its stones, reduced it to dust, and burned the grove.

Josiah turned aside and saw the tombs there in the city. He sent and took the bones from the tombs, burned them on the altar, and defiled it, according to the Lord’s word which the man of God spoke while Jeroboam stood at the festival beside the altar. Turning, he lifted his eyes toward the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words.
He said, ‘What is that rocky marker I see?’ The city’s men told him, ‘It is the man of God who came out of Judah and proclaimed these words which he proclaimed against Bethel’s altar.’
He said, ‘Leave it alone. Let no one move his bones.’ His bones were spared together with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
That night a word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
“Go and say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the Lord: You will not build Me a house for Me to dwell in,
for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt until this day. I have been moving about in a lodging and a tent.
Wherever I passed through among all Israel, did I ever speak to one of Israel’s tribes whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, “Why have you not built Me a cedar house?”
Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people, over Israel,
and I was with you wherever you went and destroyed all your enemies before you, and I made you renowned, according to the name of the great ones on the earth.
When they observed Peter’s and John’s boldness and realized that they were unlettered, ordinary men, they were amazed. They also recognized that they had been with Jesus.
Seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.
They ordered them to leave the council and conferred with one another,
saying, “What should we do with these men? That a notable sign has taken place through them is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them with threats not to speak to anyone in this name again.”
They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;
for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

But God turned away and handed them over to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you offer Me slaughtered victims and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Raiphan, the images you made to worship them. And I will deport you beyond Babylon.’
After they fell silent, James spoke: “Men, brothers, listen to me.
Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name.
With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:
‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright,
so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
known from long ago.’
The words of Amos that came among nakkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
He said: “The Lord spoke from Zion and gave His voice from Jerusalem; the shepherds’ pastures mourned, and Carmel’s summit dried up.”
The Lord said: “For three impieties of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sawed the pregnant women of those in Gilead with iron saws.
I will send fire into Hazael’s house, and it will devour the foundations of the son of Ader,

and I will shatter Damascus’s bars and destroy inhabitants from the Plain of On. I will cut down a tribe from the men of Harran, and the people of Syria, called by name, will be taken captive,” says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took Solomon’s captives into captivity, to shut them up in Idumea.
I will send fire upon Gaza’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.
I will destroy inhabitants from Azotus, and a tribe will be removed from Ascalon. I will bring My hand against Accaron, and the remaining foreigners will perish,” says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn away from her, because they shut Solomon’s captives up in Idumea and did not remember a covenant of brothers.
I will send fire upon Tyre’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.”

Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Idumea, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they pursued his brother with a sword; he ravaged a womb upon the earth, seized his shuddering as testimony, and kept his onrush for victory.
I will send fire into Teman, and it will devour the foundations of her walls.”

Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they ripped open the pregnant women of the Gileadites in order to enlarge their borders.
I will kindle fire upon Rabbah’s walls, and it will devour her foundations with shouting on the day of war; she will be shaken on the day of her end.
Her kings will go into captivity, their priests and their rulers together,” says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they burned the bones of Idumea’s king into lime.
I will send fire upon Moab, and it will devour the foundations of her cities. Moab will die in weakness, with shouting and the sound of a trumpet.
I will destroy the judge from her, and kill all her rulers with him,” says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of the sons of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they rejected the Lord’s law and did not keep His ordinances. Their vain things, which they made, led them astray—the things their fathers followed.
I will send fire upon Judah, and it will devour Jerusalem’s foundations.”
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sold a righteous person for silver and a poor person for sandals,

which tread upon the earth’s dust. They struck the heads of the poor with their fists and turned aside the way of the humble; a son and his father went in to the same young slave woman, to profane the name of their God,
and, tying their garments with cords, they made hangings next to the altar, and drank wine from extortions in their God’s house.
But I removed the Amorite from before them, whose height was like a cedar and who was strong as an oak. I removed his fruit above and his roots below.
I brought you up from Egypt’s land and led you around in the wilderness forty years, to inherit the Amorites’ land.
I took some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men for consecration. Are these things not so, sons of Israel?” says the Lord.
“But you gave the consecrated ones wine to drink and commanded the prophets, saying, ‘You must not prophesy!’
Therefore look, I roll beneath you as a wagon full of straw rolls,
and flight will perish from the runner, the mighty one will certainly not maintain his strength, and the fighter will certainly not save his life,
and the archer will certainly not stand, the swift of foot will certainly not be saved, nor will the horseman save his life,
and he will find his heart among powers; the naked one will pursue on that day,” says the Lord.
Hear this word that the Lord spoke against you, house of Israel, and against every tribe I brought up from Egypt’s land, saying:
“You alone have I known among all the earth’s tribes; therefore I will exact judgment upon you for all your sins.”
Will two go together at all unless they make themselves known to one another?
Will a lion roar from its thicket without prey? Will a young lion give its voice from its enclosure at all unless it has seized something?
Will a bird fall upon the ground without a fowler? Will a trap be sprung upon the ground without catching something?
Will a trumpet sound in a city and the people not be alarmed? Will there be calamity in a city that the Lord has not done?
For the Lord God will certainly do no deed unless He reveals His discipline to His servants the prophets.
A lion will roar—and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken—and who will not prophesy?
Announce to the regions among the Assyrians and to Egypt’s regions: “Gather upon Samaria’s mountain and see the many astonishing things in her midst and the oppression within her!”
“She did not know what would be against her,” says the Lord—those storing injustice and suffering in their regions.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: “Tyre, your land will be desolated all around; he will bring down your strength from you, and your regions will be plundered.”

Thus says the Lord: “As when a shepherd snatches two legs or an earlobe from a lion’s mouth, so the sons of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be snatched out, opposite a tribe, and priests in Damascus.”
“Hear and bear witness to Jacob’s house,” says the Lord God Almighty,
“because on the day I exact judgment upon Israel for its impieties, I will also exact judgment upon Bethel’s altars. The altar’s horns will be demolished and fall upon the ground,
and I will confound and strike the colonnaded house along with the summer house. Ivory houses will perish, and many other houses will be added,” says the Lord.
Hear this word, heifers of Bashan on Samaria’s mountain, who oppress the poor and trample the needy, who say to their masters, “Give to us so that we may drink!”
The Lord swears by His holy things: “Look, days are coming upon you, and they will take you with weapons; fiery pestilences will throw those with you into cauldrons burning underneath,
and you will be carried out naked opposite one another and thrown onto Mount Remman,” says the Lord God.
“You entered Bethel and acted lawlessly; at Gilgal you multiplied impiety. You brought your sacrifices for the morning and your tithes for the three-day period,
and they read a law outside and invoked acknowledgments. Announce that the sons of Israel loved these things,” says the Lord God.
“I will give you aching teeth in all your cities and shortage of bread in all your places; yet you did not turn to Me,” says the Lord.
“I withheld rainfall from you three months before the vintage. I will rain on one city but not on another; one portion will be watered, and the portion on which I do not rain will dry up,
and two or three cities will assemble at one city to drink water, yet they certainly will not be filled; and you did not turn to Me,” says the Lord.
“I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

“I sent death among you on Egypt’s road and killed your young men with the sword, along with the captivity of your horses. I brought your camps up in fire in My anger; yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
“I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from fire. Yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
“Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. Since I will do this to you, prepare to call upon your God, Israel!”
For look, I am the One establishing thunder and creating wind, announcing His anointed to human beings, making dawn and mist, and stepping upon the earth’s heights. The Lord God Almighty is His name.
Hear this word of the Lord that I take up over you as a lament, house of Israel:
“Virgin Israel has fallen; she will certainly not rise again. She stumbled upon her land; no one will raise her.”
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: “From the city out of which a thousand went, a hundred will remain, and from the one out of which a hundred went, ten will remain for Israel’s house.”
For thus says the Lord to Israel’s house: “Seek Me and you will live!
Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath; for Gilgal will certainly be taken captive, and Bethel will be as though it did not exist.”
Seek the Lord and live, so that Joseph’s house does not flare up like fire; it will devour him, and there will be no one to quench it for Israel’s house.
The Lord makes judgment on high and has placed righteousness upon the earth,

making all things and refashioning them, turning death’s shadow into morning and darkening day into night; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name,
the One distributing shattering against strength and bringing suffering upon a fortress.
They hated one who reproved at the gates and abhorred a holy word.

Therefore, because you struck the poor with fists and accepted choice gifts from them, you built houses of polished stone but certainly will not inhabit them; you planted desirable vineyards but certainly will not drink their wine.
For I knew your many impieties, and your sins are strong: trampling the righteous, taking payments and turning aside the poor at the gates.
Therefore the understanding person will be silent at that time, because it is an evil time.
Seek the good and not the evil, so that you may live; then the Lord God Almighty will be with you, just as you said,
“We have hated evil things and loved good things.” Restore judgment at the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on Joseph’s remaining ones.

Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: “In every square there will be mourning, and in every road it will be said, ‘Alas, alas!’ A farmer will be called to mourning and lamentation and to those skilled in wailing,
and in every road there will be mourning, because I will pass through your midst,” said the Lord.
Woe to those desiring the Lord’s day! Why is this Lord’s day for you? It is darkness, not light,
as when someone flees from a lion and a bear falls upon him, then leaps into his house, braces his hands upon the wall, and a snake bites him.
Is not the Lord’s day darkness rather than light, gloom that has no brightness in it?
“I have hated and rejected your festivals, and I certainly will not smell a pleasing scent in your festal gatherings,
because even if you bring Me whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not receive them, and I will not look upon the salvation offering of your display.
Remove from Me the sound of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your instruments,
and judgment shall roll as water, and righteousness as an impassable torrent.
Did you offer Me slaughtered offerings and sacrifices in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Raiphan, their figures that you made for yourselves.
I will deport you beyond Damascus,” says the Lord; God Almighty is His name.
Woe to those who despise Zion and trust in Samaria’s mountain! They harvested the firstfruits of nations and entered themselves. House of Israel,

all of you cross over and see; pass from there to Emath Rabba, and go down from there to Geth of foreigners, the strongest of all these kingdoms, to see whether their borders are greater than your borders.
You come toward an evil day, drawing near and touching false sabbaths,
sleeping upon ivory beds and indulging upon your couches, eating young goats from the flocks and milk-fed calves from the herds,
clapping to the sound of instruments; they reckoned them as lasting, not passing away,
drinking strained wine and anointing yourselves with the finest perfumes, yet suffering nothing over Joseph’s shattering.
Therefore now they will be captives from the foremost of the powerful, and horses’ neighing will be removed from Ephraim.
For the Lord swore by Himself: “I abhor all Jacob’s arrogance and have hated his regions; I will remove the city with all who inhabit it.”
If ten men remain in one house, they will die, and those left over will remain.

Their relatives will take them and force their way to bring their bones out of the house. He will say to those in charge of the house, “Is there anyone else with you?” He will say, “No more.” Then he will say, “Be silent, so as not to name the Lord’s name.”
For look, the Lord commands, and He will strike the great house with fractures and the small house with cracks.
Will horses pursue upon rocks? Will they remain silent among females? For you turned judgment into anger and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness,
rejoicing over nothing, saying, “Did we not acquire horns by our own strength?”
“For look, I am raising a nation against you, house of Israel, and they will crush you so that you cannot enter Emath, as far as the Wadi of the West.”
The Lord showed me this: Look, a brood of locusts was coming at dawn, and look, one bruchus locust, Gog the king.
When it finishes devouring the land’s grass, I said, “Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!
Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This will not happen,” says the Lord.
The Lord showed me this: Look, the Lord called for judgment by fire; it devoured the great abyss and devoured the portion.
I said, “Lord, Lord, cease, please! Who will raise Jacob? He is so few!
Relent, Lord, concerning this.” “This certainly will not happen,” says the Lord.
The Lord showed me this: Look, a man was standing upon an adamant wall, with adamant in his hand.
The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “Adamant.” The Lord said to me, “Look, I am setting adamant in the midst of My people Israel. I will certainly no longer pass them by,
and the altars of laughter will disappear, and Israel’s rites will be laid waste. I will rise against Jeroboam’s house with a sword.”
Amaziah, priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos is forming conspiracies against you in the midst of Israel’s house. The land certainly cannot endure all his words,
because Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by a sword, and Israel will be led captive away from its land.’”
Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, go! Withdraw to Judah’s land; make your living there, and there you will prophesy.
But you must never again prophesy at Bethel, because it is a king’s sanctuary and a house of kingship.”
Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,
and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’
Now hear the Lord’s word: You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and you must not stir up a crowd against Jacob’s house.’

Therefore thus says the Lord: ‘Your wife will practice prostitution in the city, your sons and daughters will fall by a sword, and your land will be measured out with a cord. You will die in an unclean land, and Israel will be led captive away from its land.’”
The Lord showed me this: Look, a fowler’s vessel.
He said, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A fowler’s vessel.” The Lord said to me, “The end has arrived upon My people Israel. I will certainly no longer pass them by.
The temple’s coffered ceilings will wail. On that day,” says the Lord, “many have fallen in every place. I will cast silence upon them.”
Hear these things now, you who wear out the needy until morning and oppress the poor out of the land,
saying, “When will the month pass, so we may trade, and the sabbaths, so we may open storehouses, making the measure small and the weights great and making an unjust balance,
to acquire the poor with silver and a lowly person in exchange for sandals? And we will trade from every kind of produce.”
The Lord swears by Jacob’s arrogance: “He will never forget all your works.”
Will the earth not be disturbed over these things, and everyone dwelling in it mourn? A consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.
“On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at midday, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime.

I will turn your festivals to mourning and all your songs to lamentation. I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head; I will make him like mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain.
Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will send famine upon the earth: not famine for bread or thirst for water, but famine for hearing the Lord’s word.
Waters will be shaken as far as the sea, and from north to east they will run about seeking the Lord’s word, but certainly will not find it.
On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst,
those who swear by Samaria’s propitiation and say, ‘Your god lives, Dan!’ and ‘Your god lives, Beersheba!’ They will fall and certainly never rise again.”

I saw the Lord standing upon the altar. He said, “Strike the atonement cover, and the foregates will shake; cut through the heads of all. I will kill their survivors with a sword. No one fleeing from among them will escape, and no one seeking safety will be saved.
If they burrow into Hades, My hand will pull them up from there; if they climb to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
If they hide on Carmel’s summit, I will search them out and take them from there. If they plunge from My eyes into the sea’s depths, I will command the dragon there, and it will bite them.
If they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there, and it will kill them. I will fix My eyes upon them for evils and not for good things.”
The Lord, Lord God Almighty, touches the earth and shakes it; all who dwell in it will mourn. Its consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.
He builds His ascent into heaven and establishes His promise upon the earth; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name.
“Are you not like the children of Ethiopians to Me, children of Israel?” says the Lord. “Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt’s land, the foreigners from Cappadocia and the Syrians from a pit?
Look, the Lord God’s eyes are upon the kingdom of sinners, and I will remove it from the earth’s surface. Yet I will not completely remove Jacob’s house,” says the Lord.
“For look, I am giving a command: I will winnow Israel’s house among all the nations as one winnows in a winnowing basket, and no fragment will fall to the ground.
All the sinners of My people will die by a sword, those who say, ‘Evils certainly will not draw near or come upon us.’
On that day I will raise David’s fallen tent; I will rebuild its fallen parts, raise its demolished parts and rebuild it as in days of old,
so that the remaining human beings and all the nations over whom My name is called may seek,” says the Lord God, who does these things.

“Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when threshing will overtake the vintage and grapes will darken to ripeness at seedtime. The mountains will drip sweetness, and all the hills will be planted together.
I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them upon their land, and they will certainly never again be uprooted from the land I have given them,” says the Lord God Almighty.
It is reckoned a land of Rephaim; for the Rephaim dwelt there aforetime, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a nation great and numerous and mightier than you, like the Anakim. And the Lord destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who inherited the land and dwelt in their stead unto this day,
even as they did for the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, when they blotted out the Horites from before them, and inherited the land, and dwelt in their stead unto this day.
And the Hivites who dwelt in settlements as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came forth from Cappadocia blotted them out, and dwelt in their stead.
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, above all the nations upon the face of the earth.
The Lord preferred you and chose you, not because you were more numerous than all the nations, for you are the fewest of all the nations,

but because the Lord loved you, and kept the oath which He sware unto your fathers, the Lord brought you forth with a mighty hand and with an uplifted arm, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, out of the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
And you shall know that the Lord your God, He is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments, unto a thousand generations,
and repays them that hate Him to their face, to destroy them. He shall not delay with them that hate Him; He shall repay them to their face.
And you shall keep these commandments, and ordinances, and judgments, which I command you this day to do.
All the commandments which I command you this day you shall take heed to do, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God sware unto your fathers.

And you shall remember all the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, to afflict you and to test you, that the things in your heart might be known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.

And He afflicted you, and made you hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers did not know, that He might declare unto you that man shall not live by bread alone, but man shall live by every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.
Your garments did not wear out upon you, neither did your feet become calloused; behold, these forty years.
And you shall know in your heart that, as a man chastens his son, so shall the Lord your God chasten you.
And you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God, to walk in His ways and to fear Him.
For the Lord your God brings you into a good and spacious land, where are torrents of water and springs of the depths, flowing through the plains and through the hills;
a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
a land wherein you shall eat your bread without poverty, and shall lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you shall mine copper.
And you shall eat and be filled, and bless the Lord your God upon the good land which He has given you.
Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand have gotten me this great wealth.
And you shall remember the Lord your God, for He gives you strength to gain wealth, that He may establish His covenant which the Lord sware unto your fathers, as at this day.
And if you diligently hearken unto all His commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
He shall give the rain unto your land in its season, the early and the latter rain; and you shall gather in your grain, and your wine, and your oil.
And He shall give grass in your fields for your cattle; and when you have eaten and are filled,
take heed unto yourself, lest your heart be enlarged, and you transgress, and serve other gods, and bow down unto them,

and the Lord be kindled to wrath against you, and shut up heaven, so that there is no rain, and the land does not yield her fruit, and you perish speedily from the good land which the Lord has given you.
You shall appoint judges and recording officers for yourself in all your cities which the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.
You shall pursue justly that which is just, that you may live, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you.
And when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.
The Lord your God shall raise up unto you a prophet from among your brethren, like unto me; you shall hearken unto him,

according to all that you asked of the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, saying: We will no more hear the voice of the Lord our God, neither will we see this great fire any more, lest we die.
And the Lord said unto me: All that they have spoken is right.
I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brethren, like unto you, and will put My word in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I command him.
And the man who will not hearken unto whatsoever the prophet shall speak in My name, I will exact retribution from him.
But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken?

Whatsoever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come to pass, nor is fulfilled, that is the word which the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken in ungodliness; you shall not spare him.
You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.
You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is an abomination unto the Lord your God.
You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.
Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.
A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.
And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.
And the Lord saw, and was jealous, and was provoked by the anger of His sons and daughters.
And He said, I will turn My face from them, and show what shall befall them at the last; for they are a perverse generation, sons in whom is no faithfulness.

They made Me jealous with that which is no god; they provoked Me to anger with their idols. And I will make them jealous with that which is no nation; with a nation without understanding will I provoke them to anger.
For a fire has been kindled out of My wrath; it shall burn unto Hades beneath, devour the earth and its produce, and set ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will gather evils against them, and spend My arrows upon them.

They shall waste away with hunger, and be devoured by birds, and suffer incurable backward-bending spasms; I will send against them the teeth of wild beasts, with the fury of things that crawl upon the ground.
For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter beneath heaven.
a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted,
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to pull down and a time to build,
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to beat the breast in mourning and a time to dance,
a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing,
a time to seek and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away,
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
a time to love and a time to hate, a time of war and a time of peace.

Again I saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor battle to the mighty, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to those with understanding, nor favor to those with knowledge; for time and encounter will happen to them all.
For a person does not know his time: like fish caught in an evil net, and birds caught in a snare, so human beings are trapped at an evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
“I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
You shall not pervert the judgment of a poor man in his cause.
You shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, neither shall you justify the ungodly for gifts.
And you shall receive no gifts; for gifts blind the eyes of those who see, and corrupt righteous words.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Go quickly from here and come down, for your people, whom you led out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.

They have quickly transgressed the way you commanded them. They have made themselves a calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.’
Now leave Me alone, and in the heat of My wrath against them I will destroy them. I will make you into a great nation.”
Moses entreated the Lord God and said, “Why, O Lord, art Thou angry with Thy people, whom Thou didst lead out of the land of Egypt with great strength and Thine uplifted arm?
Let not the Egyptians say, ‘He led them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth.’ Cease from Thy fierce anger and be merciful concerning Thy people’s evil,

remembering Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thyself and speak, saying, ‘I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude’; and all this land which Thou didst say Thou wouldest give to their seed, they shall possess for ever.”
The Lord was appeased concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon His people.
Behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your contention against their contention,
and it will always be stronger than rock. Do not fear them or be terrified before their faces, for it is an embittering house.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, say, ‘Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel: An end has come; the end has come upon the four wings of the land.
The end has come
upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day has drawn near, neither with tumult nor with birth pangs.
Their survivors will be saved and be on the mountains; I will kill them all, each in his injustices.
All hands will weaken, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture,
and they will gird on sackcloth; amazement will cover them, shame will be upon every face among them, and baldness upon every head.
“And you, take up a lament over Israel’s ruler,
and say: What was your mother? A cub! She came to be among lions; among lions she multiplied her cubs.
One of her cubs sprang away; he became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
and fire went out from a rod of her choice parts and devoured her, and there was no rod of strength in her. A tribe is for a parable of lament, and it will become a lament.”
In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, ‘Well done! She is shattered; the nations have perished. She has turned to me; the full one has been laid waste,’
therefore thus says the Lord: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea rises with its waves.
They will throw down Tyre’s walls and throw down your towers. I will winnow her dust from her and make her a smooth rock.
She will be a drying place for nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord. She will become plunder for the nations,
and her daughters in the plain will be killed by the sword. They will know that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: I am bringing against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north—he is king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, and an assembly of very many nations.
He will kill your daughters in the plain with the sword, set an advance guard against you, build around you, and make a palisade and a ring of weapons around you; he will set his spears opposite you.
He will throw down your walls and your towers with his swords.

The dust of his multitude of horses will cover you, and your walls will shake at the sound of his horsemen and his chariots’ wheels when he enters your gates like someone entering a city from the plain.
With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.
He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.
He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.
I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
And you, sheep, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will distinguish between sheep and sheep, rams and male goats.
Was it not enough for you that you grazed the good pasture, yet trampled the rest of your pasture with your feet, drank the settled water and troubled the rest with your feet?
My sheep grazed what your feet had trampled and drank the water troubled by your feet.
Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will distinguish between the strong sheep and the weak sheep.
You shove with your sides and shoulders; you butted with your horns and forced out every failing one.
I will save My sheep, and they certainly will no longer be plunder. I will judge between ram and ram.
I will raise up one shepherd over them, My servant David, and he will shepherd them and be their shepherd.
I, the Lord, will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.
The devastated land will be worked, instead of lying devastated before every passerby’s eyes.
They will say, “That devastated land has become like a garden of delight, and the deserted, devastated, razed cities stand fortified.”
The nations remaining around you will know that I, the Lord, have rebuilt the razed places and planted the devastated places. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face firmly against Gog and the land of Magog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel, and prophesy against him,
and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rhos, Mosoch and Thobel,
and I will gather you and all your force, horses and horsemen all clothed in breastplates, a great assembly, small shields, helmets and swords,
And the men rose from there and looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah; and Abraham went with them to escort them on their way.
And the Lord said, “Shall I hide from Abraham My servant what I am doing?
Abraham shall surely become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.

For I knew that he would command his sons and his household after him; and they shall keep the ways of the Lord, to do righteousness and judgment, that the Lord may bring upon Abraham all that He has spoken to him.”
And the Lord said, “The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has increased, and their sins are exceedingly great.
So I will go down and see whether they are being brought to an end according to their cry which comes to Me; and if not, that I may know.”
And the men turned from there and came to Sodom; but Abraham stood before the Lord.
And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulphur and fire from the Lord out of the heaven;
and He overthrew those cities, and all the surrounding country, and all that lived in the cities, and all that sprang from the earth.
And his wife looked behind her, and became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham rose early in the morning, and went to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
And he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward the land of the surrounding country; and he saw, and behold, a flame rose from the earth as the vapour of a furnace.
And when the Lord blotted out all the cities of the surrounding country, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when the Lord overthrew the cities where Lot lived.
And now, please set your hearts on the time before this day, before stone was placed upon stone in the sanctuary of the Lord,
on how things were with you: when you put twenty sata of barley into a bin, there were ten sata of barley; when you went to the wine vat to draw fifty metretai, there were twenty.
I struck you with barrenness, damage from wind and hail—all the works of your hands—and you did not turn to Me, says the Lord.
Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:
whether it will yet be recognized on the threshing floor, and whether the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive trees still bear no fruit. From this day I will bless.”
The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

The beginning of the Lord’s word to Hosea. The Lord said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a woman of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land will utterly prostitute itself away from following the Lord.”
But you, Israel, do not be ignorant; and Judah, do not enter Gilgal or go up to the house of On, and do not swear by the living Lord.
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away.
Therefore I mowed down your prophets; I killed them with the words of My mouth, and My judgment will go forth like light.
For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.
But they are like a person transgressing a covenant; there he despised Me.
Gilead is a city working worthless things, stirring up water,
and your strength is that of a pirate. Priests concealed the Lord’s road; they murdered Shechem, because they committed lawlessness.
In Israel’s house I saw dreadful things, there Ephraim’s prostitution; Israel and Judah were defiled.
Begin harvesting for yourself when I turn back My people’s captivity,
when I heal Israel. Ephraim’s injustice and Samaria’s wickedness will be uncovered, because they practiced falsehood. A thief will enter upon him, a robber stripping him on his road,
so that they sing together as people singing together with their heart. I remembered all their evils; now their schemes have surrounded them; they have come before My face.
With their evils they gladdened kings, and with their falsehoods, rulers.
All their evils are at Gilgal, because there I hated them. Because of their wicked practices I will expel them from My house. I will certainly love them no longer; all their rulers are disobedient.
Ephraim suffered; he dried up at his roots; he will certainly bear fruit no longer. Even if they give birth, I will kill the desired offspring of their womb.
God will thrust them away because they did not listen to Him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.
Samaria’s inhabitants will dwell beside the calf of the house of On, because its people mourned over it; just as they embittered it, they will rejoice over its glory, because it was deported from it.
They bound it and carried it to the Assyrians as guest-gifts for King Jarim. He will receive Ephraim as a gift, and Israel will be ashamed of his counsel.
Samaria cast off her king like a twig on the water’s surface.
The shrines of On, Israel’s sins, will be removed; thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us!’ and to the hills, ‘Fall upon us!’
you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
Woe to those rising in the morning and pursuing strong drink, lingering into the evening, for wine will burn them up!
For with lyre and harp, drums and flutes they drink wine, but they do not look at the Lord’s works or consider the works of His hands.
Therefore My people became captive because they did not know the Lord, and there was a multitude of dead through famine and thirst for water.
In the year that King Oziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up; and the house was full of His glory.
And seraphim stood around Him: each one had six wings, and each one had six wings; with two they covered their faces, and with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
And one cried to another, saying: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; all the earth is full of His glory.
And the lintel was lifted at the sound of their cry, and the house was filled with smoke.
And I said, Woe is me, for I am pierced to the heart! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Sabaoth.
Woe to those writing wickedness! For when they write, they write wickedness,
turning aside the judgment of the poor, seizing the justice of My people’s needy, so that a widow becomes their prey and an orphan their plunder.
What will they do on the day of visitation? For affliction will come to you from far away. To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory,
so as not to fall into captivity? For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,
abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
On that day Jacob’s glory will fail, and the fat parts of his glory will be shaken.
It will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed from the ears in his arm, as when someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine,
and a stalk is left in it, or like olive berries, two or three on a lofty top, or four or five left on their branches. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God.
In the year Tanathan entered Azotus, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians and fought Azotus and seized it,
then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and untie the sandals on your feet.” He did so, going naked and without sandals.
The Lord said, “As Isaiah My servant has gone naked and without sandals for three years, there will be signs and wonders for the Egyptians and Ethiopians;
for thus the king of the Assyrians will lead Egypt’s and the Ethiopians’ captivity, young men and elders, naked and without sandals, exposed as Egypt’s shame.
The Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping, lamentation, shaving and putting on sackcloth,
but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
These things are revealed in the Lord Sabaoth’s ears: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”
Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!
Whoever flees the fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught by the trap, because windows from heaven have opened and the earth’s foundations will be shaken.
For God will give rest upon this mountain, and Moab’s land will be trampled as people tread a threshing floor with wagons,
and he will release his hands, just as he himself brought low for destruction; he will bring low his insolence over what he laid his hands on,
and he will bring low the height of your wall’s refuge, and it will descend to the ground.
Now then, sit and write these things on a tablet and in a book, because these things will endure for days of appointed times and for ever.
For this is a disobedient people, lying sons who did not want to hear God’s law,
who say to the prophets, “Do not announce to us,” and to those seeing visions, “Do not speak to us. Instead, speak to us and announce another deception,
and turn us from this way, remove this path from us, and remove Israel’s Holy One from us.”

For thus the Lord said to me: “As a lion or lion cub cries over prey it has caught and shouts over it until the mountains fill with its voice, and they are defeated and terrified by the greatness of its wrath, so the Lord Sabaoth will descend to march upon Mount Zion, upon her mountains.
Like flying birds, so the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save.”
For I am the Lord God, and there is no god besides Me, and you did not know Me,
so that those from the sun’s rising and those from its setting may know that there is none besides Me. I am the Lord God, and there is no other.
I fashioned light and made darkness; I make peace and create calamities. I am the Lord God, who does all these things.
Thus says the Lord who rescued you, Israel’s Holy One: “I am your God. I have shown you how to find the road on which you will walk.
If you had listened to My commands, your peace would have become like a river and your righteousness like a sea wave.
Your offspring would have become like sand, those born from your belly like the earth’s dust. Even now you will certainly not be destroyed, nor will your name perish before Me.”
Listen with your ears, and follow My ways; listen to Me, and your soul will live amid good things. And I will make with you an everlasting covenant: the holy and sure blessings of David.
Behold, I have given him as a testimony among the nations, a ruler and commander of nations.
Nations that did not know you will call upon you, and peoples that do not know you will flee to you for refuge, because of your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.
Seek God, and when you find Him, call upon Him; and when He draws near to you,
let the ungodly forsake his ways, and the lawless man his counsels; and let him return to the Lord, and he will receive mercy; for He will abundantly forgive your sins.
For My counsels are not as your counsels, nor are My ways like your ways, says the Lord.
But as the heaven is distant from the earth, so is My way distant from your ways, and your thoughts from My mind.
Behold, I am bringing a nation upon you from far away, house of Israel, says the Lord, a nation whose language’s sound you will not understand.
All are strong,

and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.
And it will be in those days, says the Lord your God: I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.
For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.
Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.
And they transgressed judgment; they did not judge an orphan’s case, and they were not judging a widow’s case.
Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?
Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.
Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices did not please Me.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am placing weakness upon this people, and fathers and sons together will become weak in it; neighbor and his neighbor will perish.
We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.
Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.
Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.
Thus says the Lord: Call the women who lament, and let them come; send for the skilled women, and let them speak,
and let them take up a dirge over you; let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.
For a voice of lament was heard in Zion: How we suffered misery and were greatly ashamed, because we abandoned the land and threw away our dwellings!
Hear God’s word now, women, and let your ears receive His mouth’s words; teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor a dirge.
For death climbed through your windows and entered your land, to wipe out little children outside and young men from the squares.
This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
The Lord who made the earth by His strength, who set the inhabited world upright by His wisdom, also stretched out heaven by His understanding,
and an abundance of water in heaven; and He brought clouds up from the earth’s extremity, made lightning for rain, and brought light out of His treasuries.
Every human became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame at his carved things, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them.
They are futile, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not such as this, because the One who formed everything is himself his inheritance; Lord is His name.
And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah concerning the lack of rain:
Judea mourned, and her gates were emptied and darkened upon the earth, and Jerusalem’s cry rose.
Her magnates sent their younger ones for water; they came to wells and found no water and brought back their vessels empty.
And the land’s works failed because there was no rain; the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
And deer in the field gave birth and abandoned their young, because there was no pasture.
Wild donkeys stood in wooded valleys; they drew in wind, their eyes failed, because there was no grass, because of a people of injustice.
If our sins stood against us, Lord, act for us for Thine own sake, because our sins before Thee are many, because we sinned against Thee.
And you will say this word to them: Bring tears down upon your eyes day and night, and let them not cease, because the daughter of My people was utterly crushed, with a very painful wound.
If I go out to the plain, behold, those wounded by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, the pain of famine! For priest and prophet went to a land they did not know.
You turned away from Me, says the Lord; you will go backward. And I will stretch out My hand and destroy you, and I will no longer let them go.
And I will scatter them in a dispersion; at My people’s gates they were bereaved; they destroyed My people because of their evils.
Their widows multiplied beyond the sea’s sand. I brought misery upon a young man’s mother at noon; suddenly I cast trembling and haste upon her.
She who bore seven was emptied; her soul grew faint. Her sun set while the day was still at its middle; she was ashamed and reproached. Their remnants I will give to the sword before their enemies.
And if you truly listen to Me, says the Lord, not bringing burdens through this city’s gates on the Sabbath day and consecrating the Sabbath day by doing no work,

then kings and rulers sitting on David’s throne will enter through this city’s gates, mounted on their chariots and horses, they and their rulers, Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem; and this city will be inhabited for ever.

And they will come from Judah’s cities, around Jerusalem, Benjamin’s land, the plain, the mountain and the south, bringing whole burnt offerings, sacrifice, incense offerings, grain offering and frankincense, bringing praise into the Lord’s house.

And if you do not listen to Me to consecrate the Sabbath day, not lifting burdens and not entering Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, I will kindle fire in her gates, and it will devour Jerusalem’s quarters and not be extinguished.
And Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who had been appointed leader of the Lord’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
And he struck him and put him into the trap, which was at the gate of the separated upper house that was in the Lord’s house.
And Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the trap, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has called your name not Pashhur but Migrant.

Because thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving you to migration with all your friends. They will fall by their enemies’ sword, and your eyes will see. I will give you and all Judah into the hands of Babylon’s king, and they will deport them and cut them down with swords.
And I will give all this city’s strength, all its labors, and all the treasures of Judah’s king into his enemies’ hands, and they will bring them to Babylon.
And you and all who dwell in your house will go into captivity. In Babylon you will die and there be buried—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied false things.
Thou didst deceive me, Lord, and I was deceived. Thou tookest hold and didst prevail. I became a laughingstock; all day I continued being mocked.
Because I will laugh with my bitter word; I will call upon rejection and misery, because the Lord’s word became a reproach and a derision to me all day long.
And I said: I will certainly not name the Lord’s name or speak in His name again. And it became like a burning fire blazing in my bones; I am weakened on every side and cannot bear it.

Because I heard the reproach of many gathering all around: Rise against him, and let us rise against him, all you men who are his friends! Watch his purpose, to see whether he will be deceived and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.

And the Lord is with me like a strong fighter. Therefore they pursued and could not understand; they were greatly shamed, because they did not understand their dishonors, which will never be forgotten.
Lord, testing righteous things, understanding kidneys and hearts: May I see the vengeance from Thee among them, because to Thee I disclosed my defenses.
Sing to the Lord; praise Him, because He rescued a poor person’s life from the hand of those doing evil.
And say to this people: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have set before your face the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine; whoever goes out to join the Chaldeans who have shut you in will live, and his life will be spoil, and he will live.
Because I have fixed My face upon this city for evils and not for good things. It will be handed into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will burn it down with fire.
House of Judah’s king, hear the Lord’s word.

House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.
Behold, I am against you who dwell in the valley of Sor, the level land, you who say, Who will frighten us? Or who will enter our dwelling?
And I will kindle a fire in her woodland, and it will consume everything around her.
Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,
and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.

Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.
Because if you truly carry out this word, kings sitting upon David’s throne and riding chariots and horses will enter this house’s gates—they, their servants, and their people.
But if you do not carry out these words, I swear by Myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a desolation.
I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.
If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.
For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.
Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.
For grape gatherers came to you; they will leave you no remnants. Like thieves by night they will lay their hand upon you.
For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible
for your orphan to remain so that he may live. And I will live, and widows have trusted in Me.
For thus said the Lord: Those for whom there was no law to drink the cup drank it. And you, though acquitted, certainly will not be acquitted, for you will certainly drink.
For I swore by Myself, says the Lord, that you will become an untrodden place, a reproach, and a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be deserted for ever.
I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!
I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.
Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.
Idumea will become an untrodden place; everyone passing by her will hiss.
As Sodom, Gomorrah, and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, no person will settle there, and no human being will live there.

Like a lion he will come up from Jordan’s midst into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her. Appoint the young men over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
For Ammon’s sons, thus said the Lord: Are there no sons in Israel, or have they no one to inherit? Why did Melchom take Gad, and will their people live in their cities?

Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the din of wars heard against Rabbath. They will become an untrodden place and a destruction, her altars will be burned with fire, and Israel will receive his rule.

Shout aloud, Heshbon, for Gai perished! Cry out, daughters of Rabbath; put on sackcloth, be seized with distress, and beat yourselves over Melchom, for he will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
Why do you exult in the plains of the Anakim, daughter of dishonor, trusting in her treasures and saying, Who will come against me?
I am bringing fear upon you, said the Lord, from all your surroundings. You will be scattered, each straight ahead, and there will be no one gathering.
For Damascus: Hamath and Arpad were ashamed because they heard an evil report. They were distraught and angry; they certainly cannot rest.
Damascus grew feeble and turned to flight; trembling seized her.
How did he not abandon My city? They loved a village.
Therefore young men will fall in your squares, and all your warriors will fall, says the Lord.
I will kindle fire in Damascus’s wall, and it will devour the quarters of Ader’s son.
At the beginning of the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, this word came from the Lord:

Thus said the Lord: Stand in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and deliver an oracle to all the Judeans and all who come to bow down in the Lord’s house—all the words I commanded you to deliver to them. Do not take away a word.
Perhaps they will hear and turn, each from his evil way, and I will cease from the evils I plan to do to them because of their evil practices.
And say: Thus said the Lord: If you do not hear Me, walking in My ordinances that I set before your face,
listening to the words of My servants the prophets whom I send to you from early morning, and have sent—though you did not listen to Me—
then I will make this house like Shiloh and make the city a curse to all the nations of all the earth.
And the priests, false prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the Lord’s house.
And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!
Because you prophesied in the Lord’s name, saying, This house will be like Shiloh and this city will be emptied of inhabitants. And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord’s house.
And Judah’s rulers heard this word and went up from the king’s house to the Lord’s house. They sat before the Lord’s New Gate.
And the priests and false prophets said to the rulers and all the people: A sentence of death for this man, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears!
I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them in My anger, wrath, and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in confidence.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me always, for their good and their children’s good after them.
I will establish an eternal covenant with them, which I will certainly not turn back from behind them. I will put My fear in their heart so that they do not depart from Me.
I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.
Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
“How long before you stop? Hold back, so that we ourselves may speak.
Why have we been silent before you like four-footed animals?
Wrath has dealt with you. What then? If you die, will the world beneath heaven be uninhabited, or will mountains be overturned from their foundations?
An extraordinary fall has been prepared for him.
May the branches of his feet be devoured; death will devour his beautiful things.
May healing burst away from his dwelling, and may distress hold him on a royal charge.
It will lodge in his tent during his night; his splendid things will be strewn with sulfur.
Below, his roots will dry up; above, his harvest will fall.
May his memorial perish from the earth, yet he has a name on the outer face of the land.
May he thrust him from light into darkness.
He will not be recognized among his people, nor will his house be preserved beneath heaven, but others will live in what was his.
Those who came last groaned over him, and astonishment seized those who came first.
These are the houses of the unjust, and this is the place of those who do not know the Lord.”
What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.
Sober up, you drunkards, from their wine, and weep! Lament, all who drink wine to intoxication, because gladness and joy have been removed from your mouths.
For a nation has come up against My land, strong and uncountable. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth, and its grinding teeth a young lion’s.
It laid My vine waste and shattered My fig trees; searching, it searched it out and cast it away; it whitened its branches.
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured over the mountains. Its like has never existed, nor will another follow it through the years, for generations upon generations.
Before it is consuming fire, and behind it a kindled flame. The land before its face is like a garden of delight, and behind it a desolate plain; no one will escape it.
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?
