Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.

In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the Lord became jealous for His land and spared His people.
“For look, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land
and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.

What have you to do with Me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners? Are you repaying Me a recompense? Or do you bear a sharp grudge against Me? I will speedily repay your recompense upon your heads,
because you took My silver and gold and brought My chosen and beautiful things into your temples,
and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,
and I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation far away, because the Lord has spoken.”
Proclaim these things among the nations: Consecrate war! Rouse the fighters! Draw near and come up, all soldiers!
Beat your plows into swords and your sickles into lances; let the powerless say, “I am strong!”
Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Send out sickles, because the vintage is at hand! Enter and tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evils have multiplied.
Sounds rang out in the Valley of Judgment, because the Lord’s day is near in the Valley of Judgment.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.
The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.
You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.
On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.
Egypt will become desolate, and Idumea a desolate plain, because of injustices concerning the sons of Judah, because they poured out righteous blood in their land.
But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generations upon generations.
“I will avenge their blood, and I will certainly not acquit.” And the Lord will dwell in Zion.
How the gold will grow dim, how the good silver will change! Holy stones were poured out at the head of every way out.
Zion’s precious sons, exalted in gold— how they were regarded as earthen vessels, works of a potter’s hands!
Even dragons bared breasts, and their young suckled; the daughters of my people have become incurable, like a sparrow in the wilderness.
The nursing child’s tongue clung to its throat with thirst. Infants asked for bread; there is no one to break it for them.
Those who ate luxuries were destroyed at the ways out; those nursed upon scarlet wrapped themselves in dung heaps.
The lawlessness of the daughter of my people became greater than Sodom’s lawlessness, which was overthrown as in haste, and they did not labor their hands upon it.
And if by these things you are not disciplined, but walk crookedly toward Me,
then I too will walk with you in contrary anger, and I too will strike you seven times in return for your sins.
And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.
When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
Now He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up completely.
When Jesus saw her, He called to her and said, “Woman, you have been released from your weakness.”
And He laid His hands on her, and at once she was made straight, and she glorified God.
And He traveled through cities and villages, teaching and making His journey toward Jerusalem.
At that very hour some Pharisees approached and said to Him, “Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill Thee.”
And He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I drive out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion.’
Nevertheless, I must travel today and tomorrow and the day following, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.
Now there was a certain rich man, and he clothed himself in purple and fine linen, enjoying himself in splendor every day.
And a certain poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gateway, covered with sores
and longing to be filled with what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
Simon, Simon, behold, Satan demanded to have you all, to sift you like wheat.
But I prayed for you, that your faith might not fail; and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
He said to Him, “Lord, I am ready to go with Thee both to prison and to death.”
But He said, “I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you deny three times that you know Me.”

“A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?” says the Lord Almighty. You priests who belittle My name! But you said, “How have we belittled Thy name?”
“By bringing polluted loaves to My altar.” But you said, “How have we polluted them?” “By your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is despised, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’”

“For if you bring a blind animal for sacrifice, is that not evil? If you bring one that is lame or sick, is that not evil? Bring it, then, to your ruler! Will he accept it? Will he show you favor?” says the Lord Almighty.
“And now appease the face of your God and plead with Him. These things have happened in your hands. Will I show favor to any of you?” says the Lord Almighty.
“For even among you doors will be shut, and you will not kindle My altar for nothing. I have no desire for you,” says the Lord Almighty, “and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.”

“For from the sun’s rising to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to My name, together with a pure sacrifice, because My name is great among the nations,” says the Lord Almighty.
“But you profane it by your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is polluted, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’

“And you said, ‘These things are from hardship,’ and I blew them away,” says the Lord Almighty. “You were bringing things seized by force, the lame and the afflicted. If you bring the sacrifice, shall I accept these things from your hands?” says the Lord Almighty.

“Cursed is one who was able, and had a male in his flock and a vow concerning it, yet sacrifices a damaged animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the Lord Almighty, “and My name is manifest among the nations.”

Her leaders judged with gifts, her priests answered for wages and her prophets divined for silver; yet they relied upon the Lord, saying, “Is not the Lord among us? Calamities will certainly not come upon us.”
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will be like a fruit watcher’s hut, and the mountain of the house like a forest grove.
Hear now the word of the Lord. The Lord said: “Rise, enter into judgment before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.”
Hear, hills, the Lord’s judgment, and you ravines, foundations of the earth! For the Lord has a case against His people, and He will argue it with Israel.
“My people, what have I done to you? How have I grieved you, or how have I troubled you? Answer Me!
For I brought you up from Egypt’s land and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before you.
My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned against you and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from the rushes to Galgal, so that the Lord’s righteousness may be known.”
With what shall I take hold of the Lord and grasp my God Most High? Shall I take hold of Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Will the Lord receive with thousands of rams or with ten thousands of fat-rich torrents? Shall I give my firstborn offspring for impieties, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?
Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
The Lord’s voice will be called to the city, and He will save those who fear His name. “Hear, tribe! And who will adorn a city?
Is there not fire, and a lawless person’s house storing lawless treasures, and injustice with insolence?
Will a lawless person be justified with a balance and deceptive weights in a pouch?
From these they filled their wealth with impiety; those inhabiting her spoke falsehoods, and their tongue was exalted in their mouth.
And I will begin to strike you; I will obliterate you because of your sins.
You will eat but certainly not be filled. It will grow dark within you and turn aside, and you will certainly not be saved; whoever is saved will be handed over to the sword.

You will sow but certainly not reap; you will press olives but certainly not anoint yourself with oil, and you will press wine, but you shall certainly not drink it. The ordinances of My people will be obliterated.

You kept the ordinances of Zambri and all the works of Achaab’s house, and you walked in their counsels, so that I may hand you over to obliteration and her inhabitants to hissing. You will receive the reproaches of peoples.”
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart

from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God to Idumea: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent a dispatch to the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”
Look, I have made you insignificant among the nations; you are greatly dishonored.
The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”
If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.

If thieves came in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen enough for themselves? And if grape gatherers came in to you, would they not have left a gleaning?
How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things seized!
All the men of your covenant sent you out as far as your borders; the men at peace with you opposed you and prevailed over you. They set ambushes beneath you. There is no understanding in them.
On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.
Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,
because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.
From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.
Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.
For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.
One who disciplines evil people will receive dishonor for himself, and one who reproves an impious person will bring blame on himself.
Do not reprove evil people, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
Give a wise person a starting point, and he will be wiser; inform a righteous person, and he will receive still more.
Do not use force against the needy, for he is poor, and do not dishonor the weak at the gates;
for the Lord will judge his case, and you will preserve your own life unplundered.
From heaven the Lord looked down; He saw all the sons of men.
From His prepared dwelling place He looked upon all who inhabit the earth.
He formed their hearts individually; He understands all their deeds.
A king is not saved through a great force, and a giant will not be saved by the abundance of his strength.
A horse is false for salvation, and by the abundance of its power it will not be saved.
Behold, the Lord’s eyes are upon those who fear Him, those who hope in His mercy,
to rescue their souls from death and nourish them in famine.
Our soul waits for the Lord, for He is our helper and defender.
For our heart will rejoice in Him, and we have hoped in His holy name.
May Thy mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in Thee.
nor shall I profane My covenant, and what goes out through My lips I shall certainly not set aside.
Once I swore by My holiness: I will not lie to David.
His seed will remain for ever, and his throne will be like the sun before Me,
and like the moon, established for ever; and the witness in heaven is faithful.” Diapsalma.
Of David, when his land is being established. The Lord has become King! Let the earth exult; let many islands rejoice.
Cloud and gloom surround Him; righteousness and judgment are the establishment of His throne.
Fire will go ahead before Him and set His enemies aflame all around.
For I knew that the Lord is great, and our Lord is above all the gods.
Everything the Lord willed, He did, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the deeps.
He brings clouds up from the earth’s extremity; He made lightning for rain; He brings winds out of His treasuries.
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.
In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; take the lead in honoring one another;
do not be slack in zeal; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord;
rejoice in hope; persevere in affliction; persist in prayer;
